added_failures_note: Derived from the reviewed run's own gate arms. The reviewed manifest's baseline_suite field is empty, so no same-command base arm is recorded. The manifest's after_suite (revision d26d7f567, the gained head) names lane-resolution-head-gate.log: 145 passed, EXIT=0, completed true, failure_count 0, failure_ids []. The run's base-revision arm nearest the gained base is after-suite.log (revision 3f36e54b, 115 passed EXIT=0, no FAILED id). I independently reran the named eleven-file gate on a clean extraction of the gained head: 145 passed, EXIT=0 (review-delta-head-11file.log); and the same gate on the gained base tree (the head with the six added lane_gate fixture lines stripped, which reproduces 3f36e54b exactly): 12 failed, EXIT=1, all AttributeError at dispatch.py:12624 (review-delta-base-11file.log). The head arm carries no failing id, so head minus base adds nothing: added_failure_count 0, added_failure_ids []. The delta removes twelve failures rather than adding any.
call_sites: One production call site in the gained range: dispatch._peer_command now reads the fleet gate before dispatching the __supervise__ role to _supervisor_command (dispatch.py:3478), so the direct module entry that starts a per-run supervisor is held as LanePaused like every other launch boundary. d26d7f567 adds no production call site: it supplies the lane_gate document to five test doubles whose resolution SimpleNamespace previously lacked the attribute the lane-change path reads.

findings.text: follow-on (carried from review r-20261007T131212631457, independently re-derived here): the launch-path search collects a worker launch only when the process is started by a call named `Popen` whose argv derives from a LaunchPlan-typed parameter. Reproduced (review-delta-negative-control-popen-gap.log): appending both `_probe_ungated_spawn` (subprocess.Popen) and `_probe_ungated_run` (subprocess.run) callers to reckon/crew/resumption.py reddens test_launch_callers_reach_the_shared_gate naming only the Popen twin ('ungated worker launch root: (\'reckon/crew/resumption.py\', \'_probe_ungated_spawn\')'), while the subprocess.run twin is not collected. No such path exists in the tree today, so this does not block landing, but §6 bullet 2's forward guarantee is keyed on one primitive name; extending the predicate to the process-start primitives (or asserting the covered set in §6) would close it.

evidence provenance (introduced with d26d7f567): lane-resolution-combined-gate.log is stamped revision=35706b3f and reports '145 passed', but the tree at 35706b3f fails twelve of the same eleven test files (independently reproduced: review-delta-base-11file.log, 12 failed, EXIT=1, all AttributeError at dispatch.py:12624). The log was therefore produced from a working tree that already carried the uncommitted fixture fix, so its header revision does not identify the tree that produced it. Not blocking — the gained head's arm (d26d7f567) is readable and reproduced — but a base-arm log whose revision stamp is not the tree it ran is a provenance defect the run should not rely on.

The supplied lane_gate document carries only state/paused/reason/detail, while the real row returned by _dispatch_lane_gate also carries gate_path, path_check and path_check_detail. The lane-change path under test reads only .get('state'), so the subset is sufficient here; noted so a future caller of these doubles that needs path_check does not silently read a KeyError-free but incomplete row.

justifications.durability: The delta's necessity is proven by falsification rather than by a green suite. Stripping the six added lane_gate lines (which reproduces 3f36e54b exactly) reddens twelve named lane-change tests with "'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'lane_gate'" at dispatch.py:12624 (review-delta-base-11file.log, EXIT=1); the head passes all 145 (review-delta-head-11file.log, EXIT=0). The production guard the range added is also load-bearing: removing _require_fleet_gate_open() from _peer_command's __supervise__ branch reddens test_worker_spawn_boundaries_hold_and_admit[legacy-supervisor] with "DID NOT RAISE LanePaused" (review-delta-negative-control-gate-read.log, EXIT=1). I found no guard passing its own test by disabling itself. The change is test-only, so its role is to hold the mandatory read, not to be a runtime guard.
justifications.evidence: The reviewed run carries arms on disk at every stage: gate-head.log names 220eb563 (202 passed, EXIT=0); after-suite.log names 3f36e54b (115 passed, EXIT=0); followon-after-suite.log names 35706b3f (116 passed, EXIT=0); lane-resolution-head-gate.log names d26d7f567 (145 passed, EXIT=0). I reproduced the gained head gate independently on a clean extraction (145 passed, EXIT=0) and the gained base tree (12 failed, EXIT=1, all AttributeError at dispatch.py:12624). Two weaknesses keep this below the top band. First, baseline_suite is empty, so no same-command base arm is recorded. Second, lane-resolution-combined-gate.log is stamped revision=35706b3f and reports 145 passed while that tree fails twelve of the same eleven files — its header revision does not identify the tree that produced it (finding), so the run's base-arm provenance is not reliable on its own.
justifications.fit: The repair fits the module's existing idiom: the lane-change tests already build a resolution as a SimpleNamespace carrying backend, launch, backend_settings, validation, competence and authority; lane_gate is one more field a real resolution carries, and the value mirrors the open row _dispatch_lane_gate returns (state/paused/reason/detail). The production change reuses the existing _require_fleet_gate_open()/LanePaused, and the search helper reuses the existing _call_name. No parallel mechanism is introduced.
justifications.goal_fidelity: §6: the gained range routes the direct supervisor entry through the one gate read and makes the launch-path search trace worker process primitives to their callers and require a preceding gate read; d26d7f567 then conforms the five lane-change doubles to the explicit read. The repair is honest — I confirmed the head's dispatch.py keeps the direct resolution.lane_gate read with no fallback restored, and the diff is six inserted keyword arguments with no line removed, so no assertion or expectation was weakened. The fixture lines are load-bearing: stripping them reddens twelve named tests with AttributeError at dispatch.py:12624. The only shortfall is the Popen-keyed search predicate (finding), which predates this delta.
justifications.reuse: No new abstraction: the same lane-change path is repointed at a real field rather than a new double, and the production change is a single call to the existing gate reader. The one-six-key literal is repeated across five modules rather than shared from a helper; that mirrors the production shape and keeps each double self-contained, so it is a minor and idiomatic duplication rather than a defect.
justifications.scope_discipline: The gained range stays strictly inside the run's declared write grants: dispatch.py and the six test files. d26d7f567 changes five test files, 6 insertions and 0 deletions, no assertion altered; 35706b3f changes dispatch.py (+1) and test_the_fleet_gate_holds_dispatch.py (+267/-2). No docs, plan, index or sprint file is touched in the gained range, and the reviewed run's worktree is clean.
